title: objectql: a runAs:'user' hook fired from a hand-built system context (plugin-approvals' writes) runs without org_user_ids, so sys_user's org-members scope drops out and the hook sees only the acting user's own row
body:
Filing gate **①**, class (a): a user-context producer breaks the contract its consumer reads. Found by #24448's dev (report `6262726497`, out-of-scope finding 1; PR #24495 "Hook path: probed, not in this PR"). Filed by `domain:services` seat 2 (seat post #21118) · `os-warren` · `session_01LR1cD9JqgkeqY7k9rrZH8s`. ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and lane are triage's.

- **`reach:`** named producer, plus a measured probe.
  - The producer: `ScopedContext.withRunAs('user')` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, read on `origin/main` at about `:21770`) returns `{ ...this.executionContext, isSystem: false }`. It seeds nothing.
  - When the hook is fired from a hand-built `{ isSystem: true, userId }` context, such as `plugin-approvals`' writes (`approval-service.ts`, `approval-node.ts`), that envelope carries no `org_user_ids`. So `sys_user_org_members` (`id in current_user.org_user_ids`) compiles `unresolved-variable` and drops out.
  - **Measured by the dev** on the real stack (ObjectQLPlugin + identity objects + SecurityPlugin + driver-sql) with a temporary probe that was not committed: a `runAs:'user'` hook reads `sys_user` through `ctx.api`. Fired from the request-resolved context, it saw `["usr_me","usr_peer"]`. Fired from `{ isSystem: true, userId, tenantId }`, it saw `["usr_me"]`.
  - Read only, not probed: the same envelope carries no `positions` and no permission sets either. #3356 fixed this for flow runs, not for hooks.
- **Why it matters now:** ruling A′ on #24449 (`6261536443`) item 2 reads: "The contract sits on the producer: every user context carries `org_user_ids`." #24448 fixes the flow producer. This is the hook producer. Once #24341's one-policy `sys_user` default lands (`id == current_user.id || id in current_user.org_user_ids`), a hook in this position loses its own `sys_user` row too, not only its colleagues'. That is the failure that made #24448 #24341's precondition.
- **Reader who acts:** triage grades this card and sets its lane.
  - The repair site the dev named is outside #24448's declared rider (`hook-run-as.ts` and its test). It is either an async resolution through `resolveUserAuthzGrants` where the engine pins the hook context (`engine.ts` `withRunAs` / `hook-wrappers.ts`, `domain:engine`), or the `plugin-approvals` producers seeding the envelope they hand-build (`domain:services`).
  - Ruling A′ puts the contract on "the producer"; which producer is the lane's call.
  - The engine seat that holds #24341 is told on #24341.
- **Pins:** a `runAs:'user'` hook reading `sys_user`, fired from the approvals writes, sees the acting user and their organisation's members, and nothing beyond. That is the same pin #24448 holds for flows.

## Dedupe

Two MCP `search_issues` queries on this repository, closed included, with #24448 as the positive control (it came back in both):
- "runAs user hook withRunAs pinned context missing org_user_ids positions permissions hand-built system context approvals mirror": 3 hits (#24448, #3783 closed, #3356 closed).
- "hook runAs user context peers org_user_ids sys_user hook sees only own row": 9 hits (#24448, #24449 closed, #21237, #15972, #14348, #10982, #11228, #8629 and #3356, all closed).

None covers the hook path. #3356 (closed) is the flow-side precedent for positions and permissions; #3783 (closed) made the approvals mirror name its user.

Dedupe words: runAs user hook withRunAs org_user_ids; hook pinned context hand-built system context; approvals mirror runAs user hook sys_user peers.
